reasoning: I agree with the Market Analyst's neutral call: the regime is on (SPY 6.1% above its 200-day), but tech is rotating out, credit is softening and short-term volatility is rising. I approve VOO and WMT at reduced size and reject CARG. That takes the account from about 17.5% to about 39% invested ($235 of $600) and keeps the ramp toward 80-90% within the week, without buying all of it at one point in a defensive rotation just before mega-cap earnings. The Skeptic's 'keep a slot in reserve for an exit' argument doesn't count here: the risk layer blocks same-day sells of today's buys (DPZ, IDXX, and anything bought this afternoon), so a spare slot can't be used to exit them. I reject CARG on its merits, not to save a slot. VOO is cut from the full $90 cap to $60, leaving room to add after the META/TSLA/AMZN prints. WMT is cut to $70 to limit the Consumer Staples label concentration with DPZ and the risk of chasing today's upgrades. Both get tighter invalidations that can actually be checked. The cash left idle (~$365) has a reason: a neutral, 0.55-confidence stance, plus a CARG proposal whose sector and cyclical exposure cut against the Market Analyst's tilts. Later sessions should fill it with top-ranked names outside the avoid sectors once their earnings dates pass, e.g. VRSN after 10-22, or MTCH.

trades.thesis: Broad, diversified US core for idle cash while the long-term regime is on (SPY 6.1% above its 200-day, 63-day +2.69%), and the Market Analyst rates broad US equity acceptable at moderate size. This is a first lot below the $90 cap because of the mega-cap earnings week, the Iran/Hormuz tail risk and rate-hike odds; add the rest after those earnings if the regime holds.
trades.invalidation: SPY closes below ~736.8 (within 2% of its 200-day SMA of 722.32), or HYG's 21-day return falls below -3% or HYG closes more than 3% below its 200-day.

trades.thesis: Low-volatility defensive exposure (vol 0.263, beta about zero; not a hedge) in a favored sector (XLP +6.02% 21d), with positive sell-side sentiment and no earnings until ~11-19. Fundamentals pass the screen (F-score 7, gp_sector_pct 0.865) with no red flags. Sized below the proposal because the staples move has already run and today's upgrades may be priced in, and because it lifts the Consumer Staples label to about 22.5% of equity alongside DPZ.
trades.invalidation: WMT closes more than 7% below entry, or XLP gives back half its 21-day gain (21-day return below ~+3%) while SPY holds, or WMT cuts guidance at its ~11-19 report.

rejected.why: The Skeptic's serious case holds and the fixes it asked for aren't available. CARG carries a Technology label and is a rate-sensitive consumer-cyclical business, while the Market Analyst says to avoid both with the 10-year at 5.14% and hike odds in play. The claim that it is unlinked to the AI selloff comes from the Proposer alone, not from a research note. Its invalidation relies on a 10-K F-score that can't be checked until about February. The Implicator also marks it as the most volatile single name in the book (vol 0.394). Its fundamentals are strong, so it can be proposed again with a checkable stop if rates and cyclicals steady.
